summary:
Eight 12x14 modules on the kit 1/2 grid: a blue double shotgun, a pink Creole cottage under one steep sweep of roof, an ochre hipped Foursquare, a plum and cream Queen Anne with a copper-capped corner tower, a blue-grey gable-front-and-wing, a dark board gambrel mule barn, an oven-and-tank yard with a green pavilion, and a brick two-storey company duplex.
Every roof and wall colour is new to the street. Each chimney is an exterior stack set into a wall (side stacks only where the wall is 3 in from the plot edge), with a mouth into a hearth, so every module cuts out cleanly.
concept_subject: A sunny row of eight plots along a gravel-and-dirt lane in a Mississippi cotton mill village, about 1900. Picket fences in different woods run along the front, each with a centred gate, and lantern posts stand every 12 blocks. Every house sits on brick or stone piers with a raised porch. From left to right: (0) a dusty-blue clapboard double shotgun with white trim and an oxblood tin front-gable roof. Its two doors sit side by side with tall shuttered windows, and gingerbread brackets carry a shared porch. A twin brick chimney rises at the back. (1) A pink-board Creole cottage. One steep dark cypress-shingle roof sweeps down over a full-width galerie on slim dark posts. Two pairs of French doors have green board shutters, and a brick chimney climbs the west gable. (2) A square two-storey ochre American Foursquare. It has a dark hipped roof with a front dormer, a white belt course and a full-width porch on brick-pedestal columns, plus a brick side chimney. (3) The superintendent's Queen Anne, the finest on the street. The ground storey is plum clapboard and the upper storey cream fishscale shingle. A front cross gable stands beside a three-stage square corner tower with a glazed belvedere and a tall copper pyramid cap. A wraparound porch has turned posts and a spindle frieze, and there is orange stained glass over the door. (4) A blue-grey gable-front-and-wing farmhouse with weathered cedar-brown roofs and a porch tucked in the angle of the L. (5) A dark vertical-board mule barn with a red gambrel roof and cupola, a hay loft door with a hoist beam, a wagon under a lean-to on the east and a small fenced paddock behind. (6) A gravel yard with an open green-tin picnic pavilion on six log posts over a long table, a domed brick bread oven with a smoking stack, and a wooden water tank on braced legs with rain barrels beneath. (7) A red-brick company duplex with stone sills and cornice, two front doors side by side, a two-storey porch on brick piers with a gallery above, a low grey hipped roof and two brick chimneys at the back.
concept_size: 96 wide, 19 deep, 1 to 2 storeys (Queen Anne tower to about 22 high)
